lines.li: [them] We've never met, but I know your name from home.
[us] Good things, I hope.
[them,you:remembered:campbroken] That camp you helped break, mostly.
[them,you:remembered:walkedsettlers] The settlers you walked out to their land, mostly.
[them,you:remembered:foughtbeside] The day you fought beside our people, mostly.
[them,you:remembered:tradedpost] That you're a regular at our post, mostly.
[them] Nothing but good.
[them] We've never met, but I know your name, and not kindly.
[us] I can guess why.
[them,their:tribal] You stood with our warriors when it mattered, and our warriors don't forget.
[them,their:medieval] You fought in our line once, and those who were there still drink to you.
[them,their:empire] You fought beside the Empire's soldiers once, and it was noted.
[them] You fought beside our people once, and they still mention it.
[us] They'd have done the same for us.
[them] Maybe, but you did it first.
[them] The folk at our post say you're one of their regulars.
[us] It's a good post.
[them] They'll be glad to hear it, regulars are what keep a post open.
[them] You're one of those who walked our settlers out to their new land.
[us] I am.
[them,their:tribal] Then sit with me, the elders say a guide eats first.
[them] Then you've a friend in me, whatever else happens between our peoples.
[them] There's a story told at home about {FRIEND}, and it gets better every time.
[us] Is any of it true?
[them] The start of it, I'm sure.
[them,their:tribal] {FRIEND}'s name is spoken at our fires, and that is no small thing.
[them,their:medieval] {FRIEND} gets toasted in our alehouse by folk who've never met them.
[them,their:empire] {FRIEND} is spoken of well in the household, which few outsiders manage.
[them,their:hightech] {FRIEND} has a good name among our people, and they don't give those out freely.
[them] My people remember {FRIEND} kindly.
[us] I'll tell {FRIEND} that.
[them] Do, it's meant.
[them] We think well of {FRIEND} at home, whatever I think of the rest of you.
[us] That's something.
[them] Your colony puzzles my people, they bless {FRIEND} and curse {FOE}.
[us] Both live here.
[them] So I hear, and I hope they don't share a table.
[them] Keep {FOE} out of my way while I'm here, for both our sakes.
[us] I'll see what I can do.
[them,their:tribal] The one {FOE} killed has a name at our fires, and so does {FOE}.
[them] The one {FOE} killed had a family, and they know the name.
[us] It was a fight.
[them] I know, and that isn't what they'll remember.
[them] They say at home that {FOE} cut one of ours open for parts.
[us] I won't argue with that.
[them] Then you understand why the name isn't said kindly at home.
[them] Whose hand was it, when your colony put one of ours to death?
[us] It was {FOE}'s.
[them] Then that's the name we'll keep.
[them,their:tribal] {FOE} spoke ill of one of ours, and words like that travel back to the fire.
[them] {FOE} said hard words to one of ours, and words travel further than people think.
[us] {FOE} has a temper.
[them] Then {FOE} should keep it at home.
[them] {FOE} and one of ours came to blows here once, and it's still talked about at home.
[us] It was a bad day.
[them] For both of them, from what I hear.
[them,you:foe:brawled] You're the one who brawled with one of ours, I'll keep my distance.
[them,you:foe:insulted] I've heard what you said to one of ours, so let's keep this short.
[them,you:foe:executed] I'll speak with you because I must, not because I've forgotten.
[them] I know who you are, and I'd rather talk to someone else.
[us] As you like.
[them] Of all the faces here, yours is the last I wanted to see.
[us] The feeling's mutual.
